DOCUMENT:
Vendor Comparison: Standard Parcel Delivery Contract
Larkspur Home, Operations, June 2026

1. Purpose
Our contract with our current standard-delivery carrier ends on 30 September 2026. This paper compares three shortlisted carriers and recommends which should carry our standard (two-to-four-day) parcels from October.

2. Volumes and requirements
We dispatch an average of 42,000 standard parcels a month: about 70% weigh under 2 kg (cushions, textiles, small homeware) and 30% weigh 2 to 10 kg (lamps, mirrors, small furniture). Our requirements are on-time delivery of at least 95%, a damage rate below 0.5%, full tracking, and a returns service.

Damage and loss matter to us commercially. Each damaged or lost parcel costs us on average £48 in replacement stock, return shipping and customer service time, and damaged items are the most common cause of one-star reviews.

3. Trial
Between 1 April and 31 May 2026, each shortlisted carrier delivered a share of our orders, allocated at random by the warehouse management system, about 5,000 parcels per carrier. We measured on-time delivery against the promised date, damage reported by customers within 14 days, and lost parcels.

Table 1. Prices and trial performance
Carrier | Price, under 2 kg | Price, 2-10 kg | On-time delivery | Damage rate | Lost per 10,000 parcels
SwiftDrop | £3.10 | £4.60 | 96.2% | 0.4% | 3
ParcelLine | £2.85 | £4.95 | 93.1% | 0.9% | 8
Meridian | £3.30 | £4.40 | 97.5% | 0.3% | 2

On-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers during the trial, and all three offer full tracking and a returns service.

4. Cost comparison
Applying our 70/30 weight mix, the average cost per parcel is £3.55 for SwiftDrop, £3.48 for ParcelLine and £3.63 for Meridian. On 42,000 parcels a month, the monthly cost would be £149,100 for SwiftDrop, £146,160 for ParcelLine and £152,460 for Meridian. ParcelLine is therefore the cheapest option, saving £2,940 a month against SwiftDrop and £6,300 a month against Meridian, or between about £35,000 and £76,000 a year.

5. Customer contact
"Where is my order?" contacts are our largest single category of customer service enquiry. During the trial, ParcelLine deliveries generated 6 such contacts per 1,000 parcels, compared with 11 for SwiftDrop and 10 for Meridian. ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts, and at an average handling cost of £3.20 per contact this would save about £670 a month at our volumes. From 1 May, ParcelLine parcels also carried our new proactive delivery-day text message, which we were testing on one carrier before rolling it out.

6. Other considerations
All three carriers can collect from our warehouse daily at 6 pm. ParcelLine and SwiftDrop offer a 12-month contract; Meridian requires 24 months. SwiftDrop and Meridian have both handled our peak-season volumes for other retailers of similar size, while ParcelLine's references were mainly from fashion retailers with lighter parcels.

All three carriers integrate with our warehouse management system through standard interfaces, and none would require changes to our packing process or labelling. Each offers recipients a delivery-preference service to nominate a safe place or a neighbour, and each provides proof-of-delivery photographs, which our customer service team has found useful in resolving disputes.

7. Recommendation
ParcelLine offers the lowest delivery cost, met our service requirements in the trial and reduces customer contacts through its tracking app. We recommend awarding the standard parcel contract to ParcelLine for 12 months from 1 October 2026, saving up to £76,000 a year against the alternatives.

KEY (three known flaws):
1. [misread_evidence] at: "On-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers during the trial" -- Table 1 shows ParcelLine's on-time delivery was 93.1%, below the 95% requirement. The claim (and the recommendation that ParcelLine 'met our service requirements') misreads the table; ParcelLine's 0.9% damage rate also fails the stated 0.5% requirement.
2. [unsupported_causal] at: "ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts" -- The document states that from 1 May ParcelLine parcels alone also carried the new proactive delivery-day text message. That concurrent intervention confounds the comparison, so the lower contact rate cannot be attributed to ParcelLine's tracking app.
3. [missing_consideration] at: "ParcelLine is therefore the cheapest option, saving £2,940 a month against SwiftDrop" -- The cost comparison ignores the stated £48 cost of each damaged or lost parcel. ParcelLine's damage and loss rates (0.9% and 8 per 10,000) versus SwiftDrop's (0.4% and 3 per 10,000) imply about 231 extra problem parcels a month (about £11,100), far exceeding the £2,940 price saving; ParcelLine is likely the most expensive option overall.

REVIEW:
# Review: Standard Parcel Delivery Vendor Comparison

The paper recommends ParcelLine on four grounds:
- the lowest delivery price (saving £35,000–£76,000 a year);
- meeting service requirements in a randomised two-month trial;
- fewer "where is my order?" contacts, credited to its tracking app;
- a flexible 12-month term.

**The price arithmetic is correct:**

| Carrier | Price per parcel (70/30 mix) | Monthly cost | ParcelLine's saving against it |
|---|---|---|---|
| SwiftDrop | £3.55 | £149,100 | £2,940/month, about £35,300/year |
| ParcelLine | £3.48 | £146,160 | — |
| Meridian | £3.63 | £152,460 | £6,300/month, about £75,600/year |

The trial design is also a real strength. It had random allocation, about 5,000 parcels per carrier, and measured performance against the actual requirements.

On the paper's own figures, though, ParcelLine fails two of the four requirements and is the most expensive option once damage is counted. The recommendation should change.

## 1. ParcelLine failed two requirements in the trial

| Requirement | SwiftDrop | ParcelLine | Meridian |
|---|---|---|---|
| On-time ≥ 95% | 96.2% ✓ | **93.1% ✗** | 97.5% ✓ |
| Damage < 0.5% | 0.4% ✓ | **0.9% ✗** | 0.3% ✓ |

§3 says on-time delivery was "above 95% for all three carriers," and §7 says ParcelLine "met our service requirements." Table 1 contradicts both. With about 5,000 parcels per carrier, the gaps are too large to be chance:
- On-time: 93.1% against 96.2%.
- Damage: roughly 45 damaged parcels against 20.

## 2. ParcelLine is the most expensive option once damage and loss are counted

The paper states that each damaged or lost parcel costs £48, but the cost comparison leaves this out. Including it:

| Carrier | Damage + loss rate | Damage/loss cost per parcel | Total per parcel | Monthly total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SwiftDrop | 0.43% | £0.21 | £3.76 | **about £157,800** |
| ParcelLine | 0.98% | £0.47 | £3.95 | about £165,900 |
| Meridian | 0.32% | £0.15 | £3.78 | about £158,900 |

- Against SwiftDrop, ParcelLine **costs about £8,100 a month more (about £98,000 a year)**, rather than saving £35,000.
- Against Meridian, it costs about £84,000 a year more.
- The damage cost alone wipes out ParcelLine's price advantage almost three times over.

This still understates the case against ParcelLine, because it leaves out the one-star reviews the paper itself links to damage.

The loss figures rest on small numbers: 8 per 10,000 is about 4 parcels in the trial. Damage is the figure that matters, and it is reliable at these sample sizes.

## 3. The drop in customer contacts can't be credited to the tracking app

§5 notes that from 1 May, ParcelLine parcels alone carried the new proactive delivery-day text. That is half the trial period. The fall in contacts is equally consistent with the text message, and the text is being rolled out to all carriers, so whatever advantage it gave will disappear.

It's also odd that the carrier with the *most* late deliveries generated the *fewest* "where is my order?" contacts. That pattern fits the text explanation better than the app.

Even if the whole difference were due to the app, the saving is about £670 a month (£540 against Meridian). That is small next to the roughly £13,000 a month in additional damage cost compared with SwiftDrop.

Comparing contacts for April only, before the text started, would settle the question.

## 4. Peak-season risk

The contract starts in October, so the first months include peak trading. SwiftDrop and Meridian have handled peak volumes for retailers of similar size. ParcelLine's references are mainly fashion retailers with lighter parcels.

30% of Larkspur's parcels are 2–10 kg lamps, mirrors and small furniture. These are probably where damage concentrates, and ParcelLine charges more than the others for this weight band. It would help to break the trial's damage rates down by weight band.

The trial ran in April and May, so it says nothing about peak performance for any carrier.

## 5. What the figures support

- **SwiftDrop** is cheapest once damage and loss are counted. It meets every requirement, has peak experience and offers a 12-month term.
- **Meridian** has the best service figures and costs about £1,100 a month more than SwiftDrop. Its 24-month term is the main drawback. It's worth considering if the lower damage rate is valued beyond the £48 cost, for example for its effect on reviews.
- **ParcelLine** fails two requirements and is the most expensive in total.

The 12-month term is a fair point in ParcelLine's favour, but SwiftDrop offers the same term.

## Suggested changes

1. Correct §3 and §7: ParcelLine did not meet the on-time or damage requirements.
2. Add damage and loss costs to the cost comparison, using the paper's own £48 figure.
3. Remove or qualify the claim about the tracking app, and report April contact rates separately.
4. Report damage by weight band.
5. Recommend **SwiftDrop**. If the Board wants to pay for better service and can accept the longer term, name Meridian as the alternative.

**Overall:** the trial was well designed, and its results point clearly away from ParcelLine. The paper reaches the opposite conclusion by leaving damage costs out of the comparison and misreporting two of its own results against the requirements.
